newsitem.title: CHINA: China to keep gold output above 100 T in 1997.
newsitem.headline: China to keep gold output above 100 T in 1997.

text.p: China plans to maintain gold output above 100 tonnes this year and to earn 800 million yuan in profits from this sector, the Xinhua news agency said on Thursday.

China will take more efforts to use advanced technology, cut production costs and strengthen management to try to give an impetus to the industry, it said quoting officials at a conference in Beijing.

The industry will invest 1.6 billion yuan ($192 million) in fixed assets this year, one billion yuan of which will be used for basic construction and the other 600 million yuan for upgrading technology, officials said.
Annual output capacity is expected to increase by 7.25 tonnes, they said.
China aims to raise annual gold production to 150 tonnes by the turn of the century, Xinhua said.

About 400 million yuan more will be injected into prospecting this year with the aim of finding another 150 tonnes in reserves, it said quoting Jiao Zhi, director of the Gold Control Administration under the Ministry of Metallurgical Industry.
China's gold production last year was 120.6 tonnes, up nearly 12 percent compared with 1995.
Jiao was quoted as saying in January that verified reserves were 4,500 tonnes.
